verdict.rationale: The product runs entirely on user-owned hardware: you build and flash the ESP32 firmware yourself, sign the iPhone app with a free Apple ID, and point it at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including self-hosted vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp or Ollama. The prompts are bundled in the app and can be edited and rebuilt, so the whole core stack is under the user's control. Missing for 10: an explicit open-source license statement, independent hands-on corroboration of a fully local self-hosted setup, and the 7-day re-signing burden is a limitation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Any OpenAI-compatible vision endpoint works (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, cloud APIs).
Always build with flash.sh: it applies the BLE buffer sizes in hardware/hid_bridge/nimble_cfg.h.
A free Apple ID can sign it (re-sign every 7 days).
The prompts are plain text in prompts/ and bundled with the app: edit them, rebuild, done.
The board is now the AirPlay receiver and the mouse, and the agent runs in an iPhone app on the same phone.
